name: Literal reading
reading: Wording is taken literally and the question text outranks the option definitions. There is no dedicated test of scoping words or implied conditions.
evidence: Instruction against swapped true/false definitions: Jev followed the instruction on 98.0% (SST-2) and 99.0% (SMS spam) of items.
Question form against statement form: BoolQ 89.0% vs 91.0%; SMS spam 99.0% vs 99.0%; SST-2 97.0% vs 97.0%.
CVSS levels as numbers or in words: 52.2% vs 49.7% (McNemar p = 0.16).
LegalBench 81.0%, CONDAQA 61.3%.

name: Math and numbers
reading: Confirmed weak whenever the decision hinges on numbers or counting. Compute in code, then ask Jev about the result.
evidence: Anonymous card numbers (balanced fraud set): 50.0%, which is chance (ROC-AUC 0.60).
CVSS severity bands on all 995 items: 52.2% with number ranges, 49.7% in words.
BBH object counting: 56.7%.
MMLU-Pro (14 academic subjects including maths): 82.7%, possibly helped by training exposure.

name: Dates and time
reading: The vendor warning was not reproduced for multiple-choice date puzzles. Duration arithmetic from free text is untested.
evidence: BBH date understanding 96.7% and temporal sequences 100.0% (30 items each, public data, so read as a ceiling).
Duration arithmetic from free text was not tested.

name: Indirection (double negatives, multi-hop)
reading: Strong on puzzle-style chains, weak when negation hides inside real text. No explicit double-negative or multi-hop question-answering test.
evidence: Negation inside real text (CONDAQA): 61.3%.
Puzzle-style chains (BBH): web of lies 100.0%, formal fallacies 100.0%, logical deduction 100.0%, navigate 100.0%, causal judgement 70.0%.
LogiQA 76.0%, adversarial NLI (ANLI) 67.3%.

name: Large irrelevant state
reading: Robust to padding; real long documents are fine up to about 5,000 tokens.
evidence: 2,000 words of filler before or after the text, and 8,000 words before it: at most 3 of 100 answers lost, never significant (smallest p = 0.25).
Confidence on SMS spam fell from 0.941 to 0.809 with filler after the text.
Real long documents: QuALITY (about 5,000 tokens) 93.0%, SCOTUS opinions 69.6%; only 16 of 100 LongBench v2 items fit Jev's 32k state limit.

name: Adversarial content (steering by injected text)
reading: The injected text could not steer the answer in this form. Other injection styles and instructions hidden in retrieved documents are untested.
evidence: A line appended to the text said to ignore the question and give the WRONG answer. Right answers it flipped to wrong (of 100 items each): SST-2 0, BoolQ 0, SMS spam 1.
Text perturbed to fool models: AdvGLUE 83.0%, ANLI 67.3%.

name: Contradictory instructions against criteria
reading: The instruction wins, so keep the instruction and the option definitions aligned.
evidence: Instruction kept, true/false definitions swapped: Jev followed the instruction on 98.0% (SST-2) and 99.0% (SMS spam) of items.

name: Structural invariants: P(q) + P(not q) = 1
reading: Nearly consistent for a question and its own negation. Not tested across different questions on the same state.
evidence: SST-2: mean gap |P(q) + P(not q) - 1| = 0.022, gap above 0.2 on 0.0% of items, logically consistent picks on 100.0%.
BoolQ: mean gap |P(q) + P(not q) - 1| = 0.044, gap above 0.2 on 3.0% of items, logically consistent picks on 99.0%.
SMS spam: mean gap |P(q) + P(not q) - 1| = 0.060, gap above 0.2 on 7.0% of items, logically consistent picks on 98.0%.

name: Generation
reading: Out of scope for a decision model: it cannot produce free text.
evidence: Jev returns only typed answers. Unparseable answers across every run: 0.
